source.title: Towards a deeper GCN: Alleviate over-smoothing with iterative training and fine-tuning
source.authors: Furong Peng; Jinzhen Gao; Xuan Lu; Kang Liu; Yifan Huo; Sheng Wang

record.tranche_reason: Compares random and identity initialization and reports a convergence effect in deep GCN training, bearing on V4 by a different method and in a graph setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test classification accuracy across depths, not training classification error. Those accuracy results do not measure the behavior named in the claim versions. Figure 3 and its accompanying text compare random and identity initialization for newly added layers and report stability and convergence, which bears on V4. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 4.3 and Figure 3 compare identity and random initialization of newly added GCN layers and explicitly report faster convergence and improved stability. This bears on V4's initialization-dependent training speed in a new graph-network setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' initialization-specific conclusion but omits their broader conclusion: LGT combines incremental training, low-rank adaptation and identity initialization to mitigate over-smoothing and improve deep GCN performance and training efficiency. Their efficiency claim needs qualification: Table 3 reports slower GCN+LGT training on AmazonPhoto at 16 layers (1452s versus 228s).
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses identity initialization for incremental graph convolutional network training; the version describes activation-matched and orthogonal initialization methods in plain networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization choice for newly added layers: identity versus random.

fits_no_version.finding: LGT improves deep GCN test accuracy and feature separability across several graph datasets and depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Progressive layer addition with low-rank adaptation and identity initialization can reduce over-smoothing and improve deep GCN node classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3 compares training time for the complete LGT recipe against conventional training; it does not isolate initialization or batch normalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LGT changes training cost in a model-, dataset- and depth-dependent manner.

record.problems: The initialization comparison is presented in a plot without extractable numerical values or stated uncertainty. Experiments report means over 5 random splits, but the paper measures classification accuracy rather than training error.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 and other depth comparisons report test accuracy, not the training-error behavior named in the claim versions, so they were not extracted as claim rows. Figure 3 is retained only for its stated initialization and convergence comparison.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR training error under SGD or Adam, including random labels and model-size or regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized CNNs and its prevention by identity residual shortcuts.

Activation-matched initialization, measured signal or gradient preservation, maximum trainable depth attributable to initialization alone, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks. The tested comparison concerns newly added layers in staged training, rather than initialization of an entire deep network.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery above the threshold and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports a qualitative initialization comparison, without readable numerical curve values. Test accuracy, feature clustering and full-recipe training-time comparisons do not independently establish the other claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training error, random or corrupted labels, and model size or training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and width comparisons.
Plain versus shortcut convolutional networks and their training error; the paper studies GCNs and does not test the stated CNN comparison.
Activation-matched initializations, signal or gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons and its effect on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: GCN newly added layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared random initialization with identity initialization during incremental layer addition.
rows.note: The text says identity initialization improves stability and accelerates convergence compared with random initialization; the plot supplies no extractable numerical values.
rows.check: The qualitative convergence result is supported by Section 4.3. However, Cora is not identified as Figure 3's dataset in the supplied text. Figure 3 includes training, validation and test accuracy curves, so the record's suggestion that only test accuracy is reported is incorrect. Numerical convergence times, network depth, random-initialization distribution and uncertainty for this comparison are not specified.

relationships.condition: Identity versus random initialization of newly added GCN layers during LGT; dataset and depth unspecified for Figure 3.
relationships.reason: Section 4.3 explicitly reports faster convergence and improved stability with identity initialization (R1); this supports the training-speed component qualitatively.
relationships.display_finding: Identity initialization produced faster convergence and greater stability than random initialization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
